title: Bird Opening: the ideas
line: The f-pawn and a bishop on the long diagonal take hold of a center square for a knight.

steps.text: Push the pawn on f2 two squares. It takes hold of the center square e5.

also.e2e4: That is the most played first move, the king pawn opening. This lesson starts with the f-pawn.
also.d2d4: That is the queen pawn opening, also sound. This lesson starts with the f-pawn.
also.c2c4: That is the English Opening, also sound. This lesson starts with the f-pawn.
also.g1f3: That is the knight first, often a Réti Opening. This lesson starts with the f-pawn.

steps.after: This is the Bird Opening. It gives up a little against the main first moves, for play of its own.

steps.text: Bring the knight out. It watches e5 too.

also.e2e3: That frees the bishop first, also sound. This lesson brings the knight out first.

steps.text: Move the pawn in front of your king one square to free your bishop.

also.b2b3: That brings the other bishop first, also sound. This lesson moves the king pawn first.
also.g2g3: That puts the bishop on the other long diagonal, also sound. This lesson moves the king pawn.

steps.text: Move the pawn on b2 one square. It opens the long diagonal for the other bishop.
Put the bishop on the long diagonal. It aims at e5 and on toward the corner.
Bring the other bishop out so that you can castle.
Castle. Your king is safe, and the rook can join the game.
Jump the knight to e5. The pawn on f4 and the bishop on b2 hold that square for it.
steps.after: The knight sits in the center, backed by the pawn and the bishop.

summary: The f-pawn and a bishop on the long diagonal hold a center square on Black's half, and a knight lands there.
